issue.title: Bead note and +1 events record the agent's bare local name as actor instead of its globalized name
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY epic sase-14j ("Beads sub-section in the agent metadata panel's ARTIFACTS lane"), whose plan's "Memory and follow-ups" section asked its land agent to file this attribution defect. The epic works around it in its touch-index matcher (`sase.core.bead_touch_index_facade.touch_matches_agent` recovers bare names via `globalize_owned_agent_name`) instead of fixing the write site; not caused by that epic.

Bead event actors are not uniformly globalized. Notes, note edits/removals, and +1 corroborations written by agents record the agent's bare local name (`sase-157.8`, `sase-11y.land`, `013`, `00a--1`) while bead creation records the globalized name (`bbugyi200.athena.0gk`). A bare local name is ambiguous across machines and users, so another machine's reader cannot attribute it reliably.

Root cause: `resolve_mutation_author` in `src/sase/bead/cli_crud_common.py:17` returns `discover_agent_identity().name` (the local name) or the owner. `sase.bead.attribution.acting_agent_name()` already does the right thing for creation: it validates the name and returns `globalize_owned_agent_name(identity.name)`. The fix is to route `resolve_mutation_author` (and any other note/+1 author resolution that bypasses it) through the same globalization, falling back to the owner. Historical rows stay bare; readers keep their bare-name recovery.

task_type_fields.impact: Note/+1 attribution is ambiguous across machines; every reader of bead actors (touch index, history, pages) must carry a bare-name recovery workaround, and a bare name that collides across machines can cross-attribute.
task_type_fields.repro:
Scan event streams for non-email actors that are not globalized (`<user>.<host>.<name>`), limited to recent events (verified 2026-09-21, master da766b87a):

    python3 - "$(sase repo path beads)" <<'PY'
    import json,sys,glob,os,re,collections
    c=collections.Counter()
    for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(sys.argv[1],'events','streams','*.jsonl')):
        for l in open(p):
            e=json.loads(l); a=(e.get('actor') or '').strip()
            if a and '@' not in a and not re.match(r'^[a-z0-9_-]+\.[a-z0-9_-]+\.',a) and e.get('timestamp','')>='2026-09-14':
                c[e['operation']]+=1
    print(c)
    PY

Result: since 2026-09-14, 480 note_appended, 92 task_plus_one_recorded, 4 note_edited, and 2 note_removed events carry bare actors. The newest are from 2026-09-21 (e.g. note_appended by `sase-157.8`, +1 on sase-14o by `sase-11y.land`). Overall, note_appended has 2977 distinct actors: 764 globalized, 2212 bare.

payload.description: Sibling bead-event attribution defect found by the same sase-14j design audit; both fix mutation actor resolution
Both correct agent actor identity in bead events; 15a globalizes names while this task fixes reopen event ownership.
